description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral chiller asset identity, configuration, ownership, and lifecycle control record for a central cooling asset serving occupied or process loads through a refrigerant circuit and evaporator and condenser heat transfer. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.guidance: This Chiller record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: Refrigerant type, charge record, and circuit identity are referenced
Compressor, starter, oil system, and vibration condition are recorded
Evaporator and condenser entering and leaving temperatures are captured
Water flow, pump status, valve position, and pressure evidence are linked
Tube, coil, strainer, and heat-transfer surface condition is documented
Approach temperatures and load conditions are tied to the reading time
Refrigerant, oil, and water leak evidence is distinguished by location
Pressure, temperature, flow, freeze, and relief safeguards are identified
Controller alarms, BAS trends, setpoints, and overrides are reconciled
Cooling tower or dry-cooler interface condition is recorded when applicable
Electrical enclosure, disconnect, conductors, and grounding are observed
Recent service, refrigerant handling, and unresolved deficiency records are linked

items: Physical nameplate and location are distinguished from imported inventory data
Asset ID, parent system, child components, served area, and owner are mapped
Capacity, rating, configuration, utilities, controls, and interfaces are recorded
Manuals, drawings, warranties, permits, certificates, and commissioning records are linked
Maintenance plan, service history, failure history, spares, and vendor route are visible
Criticality, redundancy, outage impact, replacement lead time, and contingency are assessed

Retirement, transfer, disposal, data retention, and downstream inventory changes are controlled

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Suspected refrigerant release, oxygen-deficiency concern, or strong chemical odor
High-pressure, freeze, flow, oil, motor, or relief safeguard is active or bypassed
Unexpected electrical, mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, or thermal energy is uncontrolled
Water loss, tube rupture, flooding, or freeze damage threatens people or equipment
Starter, conductor, disconnect, or enclosure shows heat, arcing, or exposed live parts
Compressor noise, vibration, oil loss, or pressure condition suggests imminent damage
Required refrigerant credential, work authorization, permit, or recovery route is unavailable
Operating data conflicts with nameplate, controller, BAS trend, or prior service evidence

blocks.guidance: Check only controls supported by referenced evidence; unresolved controls remain open conditions.
items: Physical identity and source documents support the current register values
Configuration, location, parent-child, utility, and control relationships reconcile
Criticality and contingency reflect current service and redundancy
Warranties, permits, certificates, inspections, and service requirements have owners
Record changes identify source, approver, effective date, and prior value
Retirement or transfer includes physical, financial, environmental, and data disposition
Qualified reviewer confirms refrigerant work and leak records use the approved process
Operating readings are evaluated only against manufacturer or approved facility criteria
Water-side valves, pumps, strainers, and treatment impacts have accountable owners
Safeties, alarms, setpoints, and overrides are restored or visibly restricted
Any temporary operation has a limit, monitoring owner, and stop trigger
Return to service is authorized separately from completion of the record

blocks.guidance: Unchecked items require an exception disposition or a documented reopen trigger before the record can be treated as closed.
items: Refrigerant, oil, and water circuits have a documented final leak condition
Valves, pumps, strainers, vents, drains, and access panels are left in the approved state
Energy-control devices are removed only by the authorized process and person
Controller modes, alarms, setpoints, BAS points, and schedules are reconciled
Open cooling-load risk and temporary capacity limits are communicated
Refrigerant handling, parts, readings, photos, and service evidence are filed
